profile.stagger_pattern: No stagger. All 9 council seats (8 single-member wards + 1 at-large elected Council President) and the mayoralty are elected concurrently every cycle. Terms begin the first Monday in November. The 2016-2020 and 2025-2029 terms were 4 years; the 2020-2025 term ran FIVE years because Alabama Act 2021-297 moved the August 2024 municipal election to August 2025 and extended the sitting term accordingly.
profile.election_month: August (4th Tuesday); runoff in October (2020) or September (2025); terms begin first Monday in November

gaps.attempted: RESOLVED AS A COMPLETE FINDING, NOT A RETRIEVAL FAILURE. Seat became vacant by operation of Alabama law on 2026-05-25 when Troy Harvill's 90-day absence window (running from the 2026-02-24 meeting, after a 2026-02-10 reinstatement vote) expired without his return. The council voted unanimously on 2026-06-23 not to reinstate him (Selma Times-Journal 2026-06-24; WAKA 2026-07-07; WSFA 2026-07-16). City Attorney Graham Mosley stated the council had 60 days - to 2026-07-25 - to appoint a successor, failing which Mayor Moss must call a special election. Outcome confirmed via the Black Belt News Network site search (curl, /search/?q=...): 'Selma City Council passes on appointing Ward 1 member, instructs mayor to host special election' - Council President Kennard Randolph announced the council would forego an appointment and Mayor Johnny Moss III will call a special election, schedule not yet announced. https://www.blackbeltnewsnetwork.com/elections/selma-city-council-passes-on-appointing-ward-1-member-instructs-mayor-to-host-special-election/article_ad020aff-4218-4264-8549-fe3b64801e0f.html
gaps.notes: Lawfully vacant from 2026-05-25 to the end of the observation window (2026-08-17). No appointment was made; a special election is pending with no date set. Harvill holds the seat 2025-11-03 to 2026-05-25 and is recorded as a tenure row for that stretch.

run_log.detail: Read agent-brief.md and the Alabama + cross-state sections of state-registry.md.

2021 ACT RESOLVED - SELMA WAS AFFECTED. Selma held no August 2024 election; its next municipal election after 2020 was 2025-08-26 (selma-al.gov qualified-candidate notice; Selma Times-Journal 2025-08-26 and 2025-09-30). The 2020-elected officials therefore served a FIVE-YEAR term, 2020-11-03 to 2025-11-03, exactly as Act 2021-297 provides. Selma is NOT exempt (unlike Mobile) and NOT unaffected (unlike Auburn). Cycle calendar: 2016-08-23 general / 2016-10-04 runoff -> 4-yr term; 2020-08-25 general / 2020-10-06 runoff -> 5-yr term; 2025-08-26 general / 2025-09-23 runoff -> 4-yr term (STJ: 'will serve the next four years'). No 2024 cycle exists. seats_up=10 counts mayor + Council President + 8 wards.

NEW SOURCE, not in the registry: bamapolitics.com carries complete per-race Selma results including runoffs, curl-fetchable with a browser UA. URL pattern https://www.bamapolitics.com/alabama/alabama-elections/2020-alabama-elections/2020-selma-al-{race}-election/ where {race} is 'mayor', 'city-council-president-at-large', or 'city-council-district-{1..8}'. Note the slug says 'district' although Selma's charter says 'ward'. All ten 2020 races retrieved with vote totals and (I) incumbency markers. COVERAGE LIMIT: only 2020 exists - 2016 and 2025 slugs 404 in every variant tried, and the Selma city hub page links only 2020 races.

2025 cycle recovered from the Selma Times-Journal. REGISTRY CORRECTION: the registry says selmatimesjournal.com is 'search snippets only'. That is WRONG as of 2026-08-17 - curl with a browser UA returns HTTP 200 and full article text. However the site was migrated: dated permalinks (/YYYY/MM/DD/slug/) now render only headline+lede with the body stripped, while the same article at /news/{slug}-{importedId} returns the FULL body. The importedId is printed in the dated page's own markup ('importedId:350931'), so the dated URL is still useful as a lookup key. 2025-09-30 canvass article gives every ward, both runoff and general outcomes, and the 2025-11-03 term start. 2020-11-03 swearing-in article confirms all nine were actually seated (satisfies the brief's 'winning is not holding' rule).

2016-2020 term roster recovered without any 2016 election record, from two independent newspaper sources that each name all nine members WITH their wards: (a) WSFA 2019-07-11 story on a no-confidence vote against Mayor Melton, which prints a full ward-by-ward roll call of the vote - Randolph W5, Jackson W3, Benjamin W4, Thomas W7 (yes); Bowie CP, Johnson W8 (abstain); Bowline W1, Leashore W6 (pass); Youngblood W2 (absent); and (b) Selma Times-Journal 2020-07-22 qualifying-period article, which names each 2020 candidate against the sitting incumbent by ward. The two agree completely, and both are corroborated by the (I) markers on the 2020 Bama Politics race pages for W5, W6, W7, W8 and Council President. A roll-call story of this kind is the cheapest full-composition source found for this city.

REGISTRY LEAD DEAD FOR THIS CITY: the cross-state table's Alabama entry (EOPA audit reports at alison.legislature.state.al.us/files/pdf/eopa/audit_reports/, 'Exhibit #1' naming mayor + council) returns NOTHING for the City of Selma. Two searches, one domain-restricted, surfaced only Selma City Board of Education and Cahawba Advisory Committee reports. EOPA's own site states only the last five years are posted. Alabama municipalities are generally audited by private CPA firms rather than EOPA, so the Homewood verification does not generalize to Selma. Do not spend budget here for Selma.

ONE mid-term change found in the whole window, and it is in the current term. Ward 1: Troy Harvill removed by operation of Alabama law for 90 consecutive days of non-attendance. Chronology from STJ 2026-06-24 quoting City Attorney Graham Mosley: an earlier removal was reversed by a reinstatement vote on 2026-02-10, making 2026-02-24 the start of the new 90-day clock; that clock ran out 2026-05-25 without his return, so the seat became vacant again by law; at the 2026-06-23 meeting the council voted unanimously (motion by Michael Johnson) not to reinstate. Councilwoman Jannie Thomas told WAKA this was Harvill's SECOND reinstatement vote of 2026, implying a first lapse earlier in 2026 that was cured on 2026-02-10 - that earlier window is not separately dated and is NOT filed as a gap. NO mid-term changes found for 2019, or across the entire five-year 2020-2025 term: all nine 2020 winners are named as sitting incumbents in the 2025-09-30 canvass article (W5 Randolph 'informed his colleagues he would be retiring', i.e. served to term end), and Clay Carmichael is described as having been president pro tem 'for the last five years', which independently rules out a break in his service.

PRESIDING OFFICER (role vice_mayor, stable seat_label 'Council President Pro Tem') reconstructed in full. NOTE THIS IS A DIFFERENT OFFICE FROM THE COUNCIL PRESIDENT: in Selma the Council President is a directly elected at-large council seat (recorded as role council_member), while the Pro Tem is the internal presiding officer chosen by the council. Chain: Angela Benjamin (Ward 4) was pro tem up to 2020-11-03, sourced only as the 'outgoing Selma City Council President Pro Tem' who passed the gavel at the 2020 inauguration - her start date is NOT sourced, so her row is confidence 'low' and the 2016-11-07 start is a term-start assumption, not a finding. Clay Carmichael (Ward 3) pro tem 2020-11-03 to 2025-11-03 ('served as president pro tem for the last five years', BBNN 2025). Michael Johnson (Ward 8) elected pro tem at the 2025-11-03 organizational meeting on a 5-vote majority over Carmichael and Christie Young, and is quoted as pro tem by WSFA in July 2026. Soft boundary: the 2020 organizational meeting was postponed because of Hurricane Zeta power outages, so Carmichael's pro tem start may be a few days after 2020-11-03.

COUNCIL SIZE: constant at 9 (8 wards + at-large elected Council President) for the entire 2019-2026 window. The proposed reduction did NOT take effect. Mayor James Perkins Jr. introduced a plan in July 2024 to cut the city from eight districts to five AND to abolish the elected at-large Council President in favour of a president chosen from among five councillors (BBNN; STJ 2024-07-12 'Redistricting tops Selma City Council meeting'). It required council approval, was referred to the council's attorney, and was never adopted - Selma went to the polls in August 2025 for eight wards plus an at-large Council President, and the STJ's 2025-09-30 canvass story records 'a quorum six out of the nine members on the City Council present'. A separate Moss reorganization proposal reported 2026-08-11 concerns city departments, not council seats.

NAME HAZARDS. (1) Ward 2: elected in 2020 as 'Christy White Thomas' (Bama Politics), sworn in and reported through 2025 as 'Christie Thomas', but referred to twice in 2026 sources as 'Christie Young' (STJ 2026-06-24 'Ward 2 Councilwoman Christie Young'; BBNN 2025-11 pro tem nomination). Treated as ONE person with a probable name change, not two - no source shows a Ward 2 turnover, and the 2025-09-30 canvass names her as the returning incumbent. (2) 'Samuel Randolph' (Ward 5, to 2025) and 'Kennard Randolph' (Council President, from 2025) are DIFFERENT people who must not be merged on surname; the STJ canvass article additionally misspells the former as 'Samuel Rudolph' in the same piece that names the latter. (3) 'Kinnard Randolph' in BBNN is the same man as 'Kennard Randolph'. (4) Johnny Moss III was Selma City Schools Board President while a 2020 school-board candidate and is the 2025 mayor - same person. (5) TRAP: an abc11.com story about 'two Selma council members resign minutes apart' surfaced in search and refers to Selma, NORTH CAROLINA (ABC11 is Raleigh-Durham). Discarded, not used.

selmasun.com is DEAD as an article host: the indexed permalink /news/four-new-city-council-members-chosen-in-tuesdays-runoff-election/article_8110364a-... returns HTTP 200 but redirects to the blackbeltnewsnetwork.com Dallas County section front, i.e. the archive was folded into BBNN and old article URLs no longer resolve to their content. blackbeltnewsnetwork.com itself is fully curl-fetchable and is the best living Selma outlet. Also confirmed: bare host selma-al.gov fetches fine (the city-council roster page renders all nine seats); the stale /government/city-council/council-agenda/ path was not needed.

ACFR / AUDIT-REPORT ROUTE TRIED IN FULL AND EXHAUSTED - RECORD THIS SO NO ONE RETRIES IT FOR SELMA. Selma does publish an audit series at https://selma-al.gov/departments/finance/audit-report/ (curl-fetchable, direct PDF links): FY2012, 2013, 2014, 2015, 2017, 2018, 2019, 2021, 2022, 2023, 2024. THREE separate reasons it yields no roster. (1) FY2020 IS MISSING ENTIRELY from the series - the one year that would have bracketed the 2020 handover. (2) FY2021-FY2024 have a text layer and were extracted with pdftotext -layout across all 65-75 pages; they contain NO list of principal officials and NO named governing body. The auditor's transmittal is addressed generically 'To the Honorable Mayor and Members of City Council', exactly the failure mode the registry already documents for Washington's SAO. Greps for every known councillor surname returned zero hits. (3) FY2018 and FY2019 are IMAGE-ONLY SCANS (RICOH MP C3003, no embedded fonts, pdftotext returns 0 lines). Rendered FY2019 to PNG and read the Table of Contents directly: it begins at 'FINANCIAL SECTION / Independent Auditors' Report' - there is no introductory section and therefore no 'List of Principal Officials' page. These are plain financial-statement audits, not ACFRs. Separately, the EOPA route is also dead for Selma (see the earlier rung-3 entry). Alabama's audit-report finding in the registry holds for Homewood but does NOT generalize; Selma and Auburn are both counter-examples.

UNOPPOSED-SEAT TRAP CHECKED - NO SPURIOUS GAPS PRESENT. Alabama declares a sole qualified candidate elected without a ballot, so unopposed seats can vanish from a results archive. For Selma 2025 this is real: Lesia James (Ward 4) and Michael Johnson (Ward 8) drew no opposition and appear in the qualified-candidate list but not as contested races. Both are nonetheless recorded here as sourced tenures, because the 2025-09-30 canvass article names them as seated members of the incoming council and selma-al.gov's roster carries them. For 2020 the trap does not arise at all: all ten races (mayor, Council President and Wards 1-8) appear on Bama Politics with vote totals, so nobody was unopposed. Crucially, these unopposed wards are NOT evidence of the proposed 8-to-5 district reduction - Selma went to the polls in 2025 for all eight wards plus the at-large presidency, and the reduction was never adopted.

HYPERLOCAL / API SWEEP. selmatimesjournal.com is now a Next.js app, NOT WordPress - /wp-json/wp/v2/search returns the Next error shell, so the WordPress REST trick does not apply here. What works instead is blackbeltnewsnetwork.com (TownNews), whose site search is plain-HTML and curl-fetchable: https://www.blackbeltnewsnetwork.com/search/?q=<terms>&s=start_time&sd=desc returns dated headlines with permalinks. One such call resolved the open Ward 1 question and surfaced five further Selma council stories. BBNN is also the successor archive to selmasun.com (same publisher, Cindy Fisher) and is the single best living source for this city - recommend adding it to the Alabama registry entry alongside bamapolitics.com.

88 seat-years in scope (11 seat labels: Mayor, Council President (At-Large), Wards 1-8, Council President Pro Tem, x 8 years 2019-2026). 87 covered by tenure rows; 1 (Ward 1, 2026) is a partial-year lawful vacancy recorded in gaps with reason 'vacant'. Confidence rule applied: 'high' where a results record with vote totals or a dated canvass/organizational-meeting report names the person for that specific cycle AND a second independent source shows them seated; 'medium' where a single newspaper source establishes the holding; 'low' only for Angela Benjamin's pro tem start date, which is inferred from the term boundary rather than dated.
